text: Eithne of Connacht was a quasi-historical princess. With her sister Fedelm, she left Cruachan to bathe in the spring called Ogalla. There the sisters met white-clad monks led by St. Patrick and asked about his new religion. They asked whether his god was manly and had fair daughters. Patrick converted them, and they died to reach heaven unstained. The tale is Christian propaganda that reveals older Celtic animism.
